items.title: Compact phase-generator mixture
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, with its Borel sigma-algebra, and let $a:K\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. The **convex hull** $\operatorname{conv}K$ is the set of finite convex combinations of points of $K$. A **phase generator** is a point $y\in K$ with declared energy $a(y)$. A **mixture** is a Borel probability measure $P$ on $K$. Its barycenter and mean energy are the coordinatewise Lebesgue integrals
$$\bar y(P):=\int_K y\,dP(y)\in\mathbb R^d,\qquad \bar a(P):=\int_K a(y)\,dP(y)\in\mathbb R.$$
These integrals are finite because each coordinate and $a$ are bounded on compact $K$. For prescribed mean $x\in\operatorname{conv}K$, the **mixture energy** is
$$a_{\rm mix}(x):=\inf\{\bar a(P):P\text{ is a Borel probability on }K,\ \bar y(P)=x\}.$$
The admissible set is nonempty since every finite convex combination of points of $K$ is the barycenter of a finite atomic probability. The definition does not assert that the infimum is attained; the theorem on this page gives a compact continuous sufficient condition.

items.title: Elastic collision model and weak collision identity
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge2$. The **elastic collision set** is
$$Q_{\rm el}:=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{4d}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\},$$
with its relative Borel sigma-algebra. A collision measure is a nonnegative countably additive measure $\nu$ on this measurable space. It is symmetric if it is invariant under the exchanges $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(w,v)$, $(v',w')\leftrightarrow(w',v')$, and $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(v',w')$. These invariances are hypotheses on $\nu$, not consequences of energy and momentum conservation.

For a positive function $f:\mathbb R^d\to(0,\infty)$, write $Q(f)$ for a collision operator when the following **weak collision identity** holds for each test function $\varphi$ used:
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi(v)Q(f)(v)\,dv=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(f(v')f(w')-f(v)f(w))(\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w'))\,d\nu,$$
with absolute convergence. This identity is the adopted mathematical collision model. Molecular chaos or a microscopic derivation of it is not part of the definition.

items.title: Finite-site canonical law and narrow microcanonical shell
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix a finite alphabet $A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$, $q\ge1$, and real single-site energies $e_1,\ldots,e_q$ in a fixed energy unit. At inverse parameter $\beta\in\mathbb R$, define
$$Z_1(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^q e^{-\beta e_j},\qquad p_j(\beta):=e^{-\beta e_j}/Z_1(\beta),\qquad E(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^q p_j(\beta)e_j.$$
For $N\ge1$, a configuration $i=(i_1,\ldots,i_N)\in A^N$ has additive energy $H_N(i):=\sum_{r=1}^Ne_{i_r}$. Given a width $\delta_N\ge0$, the **shell** is
$$\Gamma_N(\beta,\delta_N):=\{i\in A^N:|H_N(i)-NE(\beta)|\le\delta_N\}.$$
When this finite set is nonempty, its microcanonical law means the uniform probability on $\Gamma_N$, and its dimensionless entropy is $\log|\Gamma_N|$. A type is a vector $t=(n_1/N,\ldots,n_q/N)$, where the nonnegative integer counts sum to $N$; its multiplicity is $N!/\prod_j n_j!$.

The convention fixes both the shell center and the law within the shell. It makes no physical claim that an apparatus has resolution $\delta_N$.

items.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck integral equation
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0},P)$ carry a standard Brownian motion $B$ adapted to the filtration, with future increments independent of the present sigma-algebra. Fix constants $\gamma>0$ and $\sigma>0$, and an $\mathcal F_0$-measurable real random variable $X_0$ with finite second moment. A **continuous adapted solution of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck equation** on $[0,T]$ is a continuous adapted process $X$ satisfying, almost surely for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$X_t=X_0-\gamma\int_0^tX_s\,ds+\sigma B_t,$$
where the time integral is the ordinary Lebesgue integral along the continuous path. In differential notation this is $dX_t=-\gamma X_t\,dt+\sigma\,dB_t$, with the stochastic differential interpreted through the displayed integral equation.

The definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. The Itô integral in the explicit representation is the square-integrable predictable-process integral of [[def-ito-integral-for-square-integrable-predictable-processes]].

items.title: Regular energy shell and weighted area measure
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $O\subset\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge2$, be open, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. An energy $E\in J$ is **regular** if $\nabla H(x)\ne0$ for every $x\in\Sigma_E:=H^{-1}(\{E\})$. By the implicit-function theorem, a neighborhood of each point of a nonempty regular level is a graph $x_i=h(z)$.

In a graph chart, use the local area density $\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(z)|^2}\,dz$, where $dz$ is $(m-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. A **graph partition** on $\Sigma_E$ is a locally finite graph-chart cover with nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_a$ supported in their respective charts and summing to one on the level. Whenever such a partition is supplied, define the candidate weighted shell integral by
$$\mu_E(g):=\sum_a\int g(z,h_a(z))\chi_a(z,h_a(z))|\partial_iH(z,h_a(z))|^{-1}\,dz$$
for nonnegative Borel $g$. Its independence from the chosen chart partition, and its equality with $\int_{\Sigma_E}g|\nabla H|^{-1}dA_E$, are proved in the theorem on this page. If $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, the **microcanonical shell probability** is $\widehat\mu_E:=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$.

This is an explicit chart-based definition, not a formal delta distribution $\delta(H-E)$. Critical levels are excluded.

items.title: Continuous ideal-gas bulk limit and finite-block bridge
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix dimension $d\ge1$, particle mass $m>0$, action reference $h>0$, inverse energy $\beta>0$, and positive cube volumes $V_N$ with $N/V_N\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$. For $N$ indistinguishable classical noninteracting particles in a cube of volume $V_N$, use the phase-space reference $dq\,dp/(N!h^{dN})$ and Hamiltonian $H_N(q,p)=\sum_{i=1}^N|p_i|^2/(2m)$. Define $\lambda_\beta=h\sqrt{\beta/(2\pi m)}$. Then the dimensionless partition integral and free-energy limits are
$$Z_N=\frac{V_N^N}{N!\lambda_\beta^{dN}},\quad\frac{-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N}{N}\longrightarrow\beta^{-1}[\log(\rho\lambda_\beta^d)-1],\quad\frac{-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N}{V_N}\longrightarrow\beta^{-1}\rho[\log(\rho\lambda_\beta^d)-1].$$
There is also the following finite-momentum-block limit. Let $M=dN$, let $G_1,\ldots,G_M$ be independent standard normal variables, set $A_N=M^{-1}\sum_{a=1}^MG_a^2$, and define canonical momenta $P_a^{\rm can}=\sqrt{m/\beta}\,G_a$ and shell-prepared momenta $P_a^{\rm sh}=\sqrt{m/\beta}\,G_a/\sqrt{A_N}$. The shell-prepared vector has exactly energy $dN/(2\beta)$, and for every fixed $r$ and bounded continuous $\psi:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R$,
$$\mathbb E\psi(P_1^{\rm sh},\ldots,P_r^{\rm sh})\longrightarrow\mathbb E\psi(P_1^{\rm can},\ldots,P_r^{\rm can}).$$
This is weak convergence for each fixed block in this free-particle model. The shell preparation is the stated normalized-Gaussian construction, and no finite-width shell or interacting-gas equivalence is asserted.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-continuous-ideal-gas-block-limit.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Hamiltonian volume, recurrence, and ergodic scope
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a smooth $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and $H\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, with Hamiltonian field defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$. Wherever its local flow $\phi_t$ is defined, it preserves the symplectic form and the volume measure $m$ determined by $\omega^n/n!$. No completeness is asserted. For a region $R$ on which a nonzero-time map $T=\phi_\tau$ and all its iterates are defined, $T$ is a measure-preserving transformation. If $m(R)<\infty$, then for every measurable $E\subseteq R$, almost every point of $E$ returns to $E$ infinitely often under forward iteration.

If $m(R)=1$ and $T$ is ergodic, then for every $f\in L^1(R,m)$ the averages $N^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}f(T^jx)$ converge almost everywhere and in $L^1$ to $\int_Rf\,dm$. Without ergodicity, the limit is the invariant conditional expectation supplied by Birkhoff's theorem, not necessarily the space mean. Finally, if each stated time map $\phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism of a finite invariant region $R$, a density $p_0\ge0$ with $\int_Rp_0\,dm=1$ and $\int_R|p_0\log p_0|\,dm<\infty$ transports by $p_t=p_0\circ\phi_{-t}$ with conserved fine-grained entropy $-k_B\int_Rp_t\log p_t\,dm$, using $0\log0=0$. Volume preservation alone does not imply ergodicity or a time-average/ensemble identity.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Attainment and finite support for compact continuous mixtures
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty compact, $d\ge1$, and $a:K\to\mathbb R$ continuous. Define $a_{\rm mix}$ as in [[def-tdmath-mixture-generator-space-and-energy]]. Then for every $x\in\operatorname{conv}K$ the infimum defining $a_{\rm mix}(x)$ is attained by a Borel probability measure supported on at most $d+1$ points. The function $a_{\rm mix}$ is lower semicontinuous and convex on $\operatorname{conv}K$, and is the greatest convex function on $\operatorname{conv}K$ bounded above by $a$ on $K$. Minimizing over all Borel probabilities on $K$ gives the same attained value as minimizing over finite mixtures. This is a mathematical compactness result; it makes no phase-preparation or equilibrium postulate.

items.title: Finite-site microcanonical and canonical block equivalence
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$, $q\ge1$, have real energies $e_j$, and fix finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Set $Z_1=\sum_j e^{-\beta e_j}$, $p_j=e^{-\beta e_j}/Z_1>0$, and $E=\sum_jp_je_j$. For each $N\ge1$, let $\delta_N\ge q\sum_{j=1}^q|e_j|$ and $\delta_N/N\to0$. Define the shell $\Gamma_N=\{i\in A^N:|\sum_{r=1}^Ne_{i_r}-NE|\le\delta_N\}$ and the uniform law on that shell. For probability laws $\mu,\nu$ on the finite set $A^k$, total variation distance means $\frac12\sum_{x\in A^k}|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|$. Then $\Gamma_N$ is nonempty for every $N$; for each fixed $k\ge1$, the first $k$-site marginal (for $N\ge k$) converges in that distance to $p^{\otimes k}$; and
$$\frac1N\log|\Gamma_N|\longrightarrow H(p):=-\sum_{j=1}^qp_j\log p_j.$$
The conclusion is for this finite alphabet, additive energy, exact shell width and uniform shell law. It does not assert finite-size equality or equivalence for interacting or continuous models.

items.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck equation, transition law, and fluctuations
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the filtered probability space, Brownian increment hypothesis, and initial data of [[def-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-equation]], including $\mathbb E X_0^2<\infty$ and future increments independent of $\mathcal F_0$. For $\gamma,\sigma>0$, on every finite time interval the process
$$X_t=e^{-\gamma t}X_0+\sigma e^{-\gamma t}\int_0^t e^{\gamma s}\,dB_s$$
has a continuous adapted version, solves the stated Ornstein–Uhlenbeck integral equation, and is the unique continuous solution driven by the same $(X_0,B)$. Put $V=\sigma^2/(2\gamma)$. For $0\le s<t$, its transition law conditional on $\mathcal F_s$ is normal with mean $e^{-\gamma(t-s)}X_s$ and variance $V(1-e^{-2\gamma(t-s)})$. Consequently
$$\mathbb E X_t=e^{-\gamma t}\mathbb E X_0,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(X_t)=e^{-2\gamma t}\operatorname{Var}(X_0)+V(1-e^{-2\gamma t}).$$
From any such initial law, $X_t$ converges in distribution to $N(0,V)$. If $X_0\sim N(0,V)$ and is independent of future Brownian increments, the process is stationary Gaussian with covariance $C(\tau)=Ve^{-\gamma|\tau|}$, and its transition kernel satisfies detailed balance with the $N(0,V)$ density. Its transition density solves the Fokker–Planck equation for positive time. Under the convention $S(\omega)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}C(\tau)e^{i\omega\tau}\,d\tau$, the stationary spectrum and time-average bound are
$$S(\omega)=\frac{V\gamma}{\pi(\gamma^2+\omega^2)},\qquad\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1T\int_0^T X_t\,dt\right)\le\frac{2V}{\gamma T}.$$
All these statements concern the specified linear stochastic model. An Einstein relation between $\sigma$ and a physical bath temperature would be an additional physical postulate.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-model.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Conditional Boltzmann entropy inequality and equality form
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\mathbb T^d$ be a spatial rectangle with opposite faces identified, $d\ge2$, and let $I$ be an open time interval. Suppose $f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\times I\to(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ in space and time and $C^2$ in velocity. Fix a positive reference density $f_{\rm ref}$ with the same units as $f$. Assume $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\log(f/f_{\rm ref})|$ are integrable, and assume an integrable envelope on every compact time interval justifying differentiation of the entropy integral and every displayed collision integral. Let $Q$ and the symmetric collision measure $\nu$ satisfy the weak identity in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]] for tests $1$ and $\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$, with absolute convergence, and suppose
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_r f=Q(f).$$
Then for $H[f](t)=\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv\,dr$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}H[f](t)=-\frac14\int_\Omega\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)(\log A-\log B)\,d\nu\,dr\le0,\qquad A=f(r,v,t)f(r,w,t),\quad B=f(r,v',t)f(r,w',t).$$
The integrand is nonnegative because $\log$ is strictly increasing. Equality in the entropy-production integral holds exactly when $A=B$ for $\nu$-almost every collision at almost every $r$. Under the additional assumptions that $\nu$ is locally finite, has full support on $Q_{\rm el}$, and $f$ is positive and $C^2$ in $v$, this balance implies for almost every $r$ that
$$\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{\rm ref})=\alpha(r,t)+b(r,t)\cdot v+\frac{\lambda(r,t)}2|v|^2.$$
If $f(r,\cdot,t)$ is integrable over $\mathbb R^d$, then $\lambda(r,t)<0$, so its velocity profile is Maxwellian. Conversely, every profile of this form has zero collision entropy production. The weak collision identity is an explicit model hypothesis; this is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a PDE existence theorem.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-regular-collision-entropy.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Coarea and invariant measure on compact regular energy shells
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

items.title: Trace-norm Cesàro dephasing for a discrete Gibbs spectrum
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the exact first-clause interface of [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]]: a nonzero complex Hilbert space has a finite or countable complete orthonormal energy eigenbasis $(u_j)$ for a self-adjoint semibounded $A$, with each energy eigenspace finite-dimensional. The supplier is a current draft whose statement and complete argument have been inspected; this theorem is conditional on that interface and does not claim its independent acceptance. Let $\hbar>0$, define $U_tu_j=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}u_j$, and extend linearly and continuously. For any positive trace-class density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, set $\rho_t=U_t\rho U_t^*$. If $P_E$ denotes the projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$, then the trace-norm Riemann average
$$\bar\rho_T:=\frac1T\int_0^T\rho_t\,dt$$
converges as $T\to\infty$ to
$$\rho_{\rm diag}:=\sum_E P_E\rho P_E$$
in trace norm. The full degenerate energy blocks are retained. Thus expectations of every bounded observable converge to their diagonal-ensemble values. This asserts Cesàro convergence, not convergence of $\rho_t$ at individual late times, and is restricted to the stated discrete trace-class spectrum.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Pure-state entropy and entropy of a dephased average
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Use $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with $\langle z,w\rangle=z_1\overline{w_1}+z_2\overline{w_2}$, linear in the first argument, and $u_1=(1,0)$, $u_2=(0,1)$. Choose real $E_1\ne E_2$ and define the self-adjoint energy operator $A(z_1,z_2)=(E_1z_1,E_2z_2)$. Fix $\hbar>0$, set $U_tu_j=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}u_j$, and define $P_jz=\langle z,u_j\rangle u_j$, $\rho_t=U_t\rho U_t^*$ and $\bar\rho_T=T^{-1}\int_0^T\rho_t\,dt$. Let $\psi=(u_1+u_2)/\sqrt2$, $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$. Define the finite-dimensional entropy of a density matrix with eigenvalues $p_i$ as $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_i p_i\log p_i$, with $0\log0=0$ and fixed $k_B>0$. Every instantaneous unitary state $\rho_t$ is pure and has entropy zero. The Cesàro states converge to $\rho_{\rm diag}=(P_1+P_2)/2$, whose entropy is $k_B\log2$. In fact $S(\bar\rho_T)\to k_B\log2$, whereas $T^{-1}\int_0^T S(\rho_t)\,dt=0$ for every $T$. Entropy of the averaged state and average instantaneous entropy are distinct quantities.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete argument is in items/ex-tdmath-pure-state-versus-average-entropy.md and its proof contract.
